definition: Symbolic logic is a mathematical form of logic, using symbols to express thought and reasoning. In this source, it appears as the kind of logic treated in George Boole’s pioneering mathematical work on the laws of thought.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Boole, George; pinned source text

reasons: The phrase "using symbols to express thought and reasoning" is not supported by the packet; the source only identifies Boole’s work as an early treatise in "mathematical or symbolic logic."

The definition states: “Symbolic logic is a mathematical form of logic, using symbols to express thought and reasoning.” The provided packet does not define symbolic logic or describe it as using symbols to express thought/reasoning.

The definition says it “appears as the kind of logic treated in George Boole’s pioneering mathematical work…”. The packet only anchors Boole as an English mathematician/logician and notes that his work *An Investigation into the Laws of Thought* was the first elaborate treatise in mathematical or symbolic logic; it does not support the characterization “pioneering” or explicitly frames the term as “the kind of logic treated” (beyond that general anchor).
